name: Feral File Archive
description: Copies of the artworks and records Feral File preserves, and the contracts Feral File deployed. Each copy has a content identifier (CID), an address made from its files' contents, which IPFS software uses to check that what it downloads matches; each contract is listed by its address. Anyone can keep a copy by pinning a CID, and every independent copy helps preserve the works. Published by Feral File; the Feral File Archive Registry on Ethereum records which version of this document is current.

collections.description: Files from a2p (2019–2020), the artist-to-artist experiment Feral File grew out of: the media of its 144 works across its two versions and its trade originals, checked byte for byte against the source. Its own archive is at https://a2p.feralfile.com.

The retired Bitmark blockchain (2014–2025), kept the way its maintainers documented: the chain's data, and the proof file that checks it against a root recorded on Ethereum and timestamped on Bitcoin. How to check it: https://github.com/bitmark-inc/bitmarkd/wiki/bitmark-archive

The streaming playlists three video works first pointed to: FERAL FONT and Some Last Questions in FeralVerse, and Rewilded Topography #1 in On Screen Presence. Each CID holds the playlist file alone, without the video it lists, so the works could not play from it; their token metadata was updated to point to complete video files. The playlists are kept as the works' original references.

collections.description: Files recovered from Aorist, a digital-art initiative that stopped operating; Feral File migrated its collections and stewards the works. Everything that survived in Aorist's file storage: originals, display copies, videos and its two IPFS stores, checked byte for byte against the source. Each CID holds one storage folder, named in parentheses, except the last, which holds three remaining files.

The five full-resolution originals (3840 × 6827 pixels) of Refik Anadol's Machine Hallucinations — Coral — Generative AI Data Painting A–E, recovered from the Aorist archive and checked byte for byte; Feral File stewards them. Each CID holds one file.

collections.description: The Feral File Retrospective, Feral File's second anniversary (June 28 to July 12, 2023): the signed playlists of its two exhibitions, The Experiment and Feral File 1.0; the retrospective's own website, 162 files, as Feral File served it; and the conversation artists and collectors had in the chat beside it, the 100 messages that site kept, each with its time, its sender's address and the name the chat showed. The page is at https://feralfile.com/retrospective.

The contracts Feral File deployed on Ethereum and Tezos, except one registry that has never been used, and what each one is, so anyone indexing Feral File's works can tell which deployment is current. Status: live, the contract of record for its works or a tool in use; completed, a tool that did its job and stopped, holding no works; abandoned, deployed and then replaced or never used, with its replacement named where there is one. Kind: exhibition; annex, a section of an exhibition's page; partner-edition, minted for someone else's event; stewarded, the Aorist and a2p collections Feral File keeps; minted-for-artist, minted at an artist's request outside any exhibition; lot, a token that stood in for an auction lot, not an artwork; infrastructure; test, an internal deployment never published. The Monopoly Set entry names its token and the CIDs of its metadata and image.
